headline: US reviews Black Sea ceasefire idea to protect grain and energy shipments
body:
What happened: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said at a news conference in Atlanta, where G20 foreign ministers were meeting, that interest in a narrow Black Sea truce is growing internationally. The aim would be to let Russia and Ukraine move energy and grain without interference. Washington is looking at proposals put forward by Turkey and India to get grain flowing. Rubio argued that disrupted food and energy supplies threaten the wider world, while acknowledging that such a truce would not end the war itself.

Reported by: Reuters. Also covered by Al-Monitor.

headline: EU and Canada agree deadline for defining new associate membership
body:
What happened: At a summit in Montreal, the European Union set a target of next year for settling the details of a proposed associate membership for Canada. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said the coming months would determine the scope of this new arrangement, while European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen acknowledged that geography rules out full membership but said she wanted ties raised as high as possible. The two sides also signed several agreements covering investment, digital trade, competition, supercomputing and border security. Carney first floated the idea in September, as Canada's trade dispute with the United States, which has included US tariffs on Canadian goods, pushed Ottawa to diversify its partners.

Reported by: Jerusalem Post. Also covered by Politico Europe.

headline: Kallas warns Putin's possible G20 return would normalise Russian abuses
body:
What happened: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said that a possible appearance by Vladimir Putin at a December G20 summit in the United States would normalise what she called daily war crimes in Ukraine. Putin has not confirmed whether he will attend; his last in-person G20 meeting was in 2019. Kallas also objected to Russian foreign minister Sergei Lavrov's presence at a G20 ministerial in Atlanta, where European officials declined to pose beside him for a group photo, which was cancelled. She welcomed a U.S. decision to sell 500 Patriot interceptors to Ukraine and urged tougher sanctions on Russia.

Reported by: Politico Europe

headline: Russian security service says Washington flagged a possible attack on Moscow
body:
What happened: Russia's Federal Security Service, the FSB, says the United States passed on a warning that an attack on Moscow was possible. The FSB presented the claim as a sign of Washington's awareness of threats in the Russian capital. The details of the alleged warning, including its timing and the nature of the threat, could not be independently verified from the available material.

The claim comes from a Russian agency and has not been confirmed by US officials in the available reporting. Moscow has frequently accused Western governments of stoking tensions, so the statement should be read with that context in mind.

Reported by: Reuters. Also covered by Xinhua, The Hindu.

headline: Iran's new supreme leader orders military readiness against any renewed US or Israeli strikes
body:
What happened: Iran's supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, has warned Washington and Israel against resuming attacks. In a statement he directed the armed forces to update their target lists so that all US and Israeli assets, tangible and intangible, fall within striking range, and said Tehran would set the timing and terms of any future conflict. Separately, Iranian state media said two fishermen were missing and two others hurt after an incident in the Strait of Hormuz, which Iran blamed on the United States; the two missing men were later reported found. Diplomatic contacts, including Qatari mediation, continue in an effort to prevent renewed fighting.

Reported by: AP. Also covered by France 24, The New Arab, Asharq Al-Awsat, Middle East Eye.

headline: Competing US and Russian Western Sahara drafts fail at UN Security Council
body:
What happened: Both a US-backed resolution and a rival Russian draft on Western Sahara failed at the UN Security Council. Russia used its veto against the US text, which had won support from 11 of the council's 15 members, and the Russian alternative then fell short of the nine votes required. The mandate of the UN mission MINURSO expires Saturday unless a last-minute deal is reached. The US draft would have extended the mission for a year, dropped the word referendum, and made Morocco's autonomy plan the sole basis for talks. Russia opposed it as favouring one party.

Reported by: Al Jazeera. Also covered by Reuters, AP, Arab News, Middle East Eye.

headline: Damascus weighs joining Saudi-Turkish-Pakistani mutual defence pact
body:
What happened: Syria's foreign minister, Asaad al-Shaibani, said at a security conference in Bahrain that Damascus is discussing whether to join the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement. The pact, signed in August by Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan, treats an attack on one member as an attack on all three. Al-Shaibani also backed Yemen's internationally recognised government in its fight against the Houthis and accused Israel of carrying out more than 1,000 strikes on Syria in under two years, killing dozens.

He framed regional security as needing joint deterrence and defence systems. Al-Shaibani did not give a timeline for any decision on joining the alliance.

Reported by: Al Jazeera. Also covered by The National, The New Arab, Daily Sabah, Dawn.

headline: G20 foreign ministers split over Russian attendance at US talks
body:
What happened: Foreign ministers from the G20 ended two days of meetings in the United States without agreeing on several major global security questions. Russia's foreign minister, Sergei Lavrov, took part, and European ministers confronted him over the war in Ukraine. The European delegates declined to join him for the group's traditional photograph. On the margins, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio signed an Arctic cooperation agreement with Japan and South Korea and confirmed American involvement in the 2030 World Expo in Riyadh.

Reported by: France 24. Also covered by Reuters, BBC News, Al Jazeera, The Guardian.

headline: Ethiopian drone strikes reportedly kill at least 25 civilians in north
body:
What happened: Multiple drone strikes in northern Ethiopia since Thursday have reportedly killed at least 25 civilians, including children, according to witnesses and a medical source cited by AFP. Four strikes reportedly hit a camp for displaced people in Amhara, about 400 kilometres northeast of Addis Ababa, as students were heading home from school. A further strike in Tigray reportedly hit a lorry carrying grain, then struck people gathering the spilled grain, killing at least 11. The Ethiopian army did not respond to requests for comment, and the death tolls could not be independently confirmed.

Reported by: Africanews. Also covered by Reuters, France 24 Africa, Arab News, The New Arab.

headline: Oil flows from the Gulf recover, but prices stay high amid war risk
body:
What happened: Crude exports from Gulf producers reached 24.6 million barrels per day in the week to October 18, above the pre-war average, according to the market intelligence firm Kpler. Brent crude nonetheless climbed to around $117 a barrel, its highest since April and more than 60 percent above pre-war levels, as traders priced in fears of renewed fighting in the US-Israel war on Iran and shrinking inventories.

Analysts say shipments are moving through ship-to-ship transfers and bypass pipelines via Saudi Arabia and the UAE, but at far higher cost, with freight rates up to about ten times normal. Attacks on commercial vessels in October were the deadliest of the war so far, and the IEA says global stocks sit 509 million barrels below pre-war levels.

Reported by: Reuters. Also covered by AP, Al Jazeera, The Guardian, Le Monde.

headline: Jordan says it repelled 14 armed men trying to cross from Syria
body:
What happened: Jordan's armed forces said border guards turned back a group of 14 armed individuals trying to enter northern Jordan from Syria on Friday. The army said the group came under heavy fire, suffered numerous casualties, and that survivors retreated into Syria. Ties between the two neighbours are strained after Jordanian strikes in southern Syria, which Syria says killed seven people, including three children and a woman. Jordan expressed regret over the civilian deaths and has linked the strikes to a deadly church attack last week.

Reported by: Reuters. Also covered by Asharq Al-Awsat.

headline: Egypt warns renewed US-Iran fighting would be deadlier and lead nowhere
body:
What happened: Egypt's foreign minister, Badr Abdelatty, said he is deeply concerned that a fresh round of hostilities between the United States and Iran would be more destructive, speaking at a security conference in Bahrain. He argued that lessons from earlier fighting should be learned. An June interim deal has not produced a lasting ceasefire or restored normal shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Iran has proposed lifting the US blockade of its ports in return for reopening the strait within a week, while Qatari mediators are back in Tehran, though the two sides disagree on whether nuclear talks or blockade and sanctions relief should come first.

Reported by: Reuters. Also covered by Asharq Al-Awsat, Al-Monitor, Jerusalem Post.

headline: Doubts grow over Venezuela oilfield deal's promised output surge
body:
What happened: A deal Washington has described as the largest oil transaction in history would hand 17 Venezuelan oilfields, reportedly holding about 64 billion barrels, to one company. That firm, North American Blue Energy Partners, is led by Venezuelan businessman Alejandro Betancourt, who until recently was the subject of U.S. money-laundering inquiries involving funds taken from state oil company PDVSA. Under the arrangement the United States would take a 35% stake in the parent company and gain the right to buy 20% of output at production cost. The company says it will raise output from about 224,000 barrels a day in mid-October to more than 1 million.

Reported by: Japan Times. Also covered by Reuters.

headline: Drone strike sets fire to Ufa refinery, damaging key processing unit
body:
What happened: Drones struck Ufa, the capital of Bashkortostan in Russia, overnight on 30-31 October, sparking a fire at the Bashneft-Novoil refinery. Citing eyewitness photos, an analyst for the Russian outlet Astra believes the L-35 catalytic reforming unit, which makes high-octane petrol components and hydrogen used to clean fuel, is the part on fire. The monitoring channel Exilenova+ reported three separate fires at what it believes are two refineries in the city. Neither claim has been independently confirmed.

Reported by: Ukrainska Pravda. Also covered by Al Jazeera, Politico Europe, Kyiv Independent, Euronews.

headline: Pakistan's military cautiously upbeat about its Iran-US mediation role
body:
What happened: Pakistan's army spokesman, Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry, said the military is cautiously optimistic about its mediation between Iran and the United States. Army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir has travelled to Tehran twice this month, most recently on Monday with Saudi and Turkish officials. Chaudhry declined to disclose what was discussed or whether Washington backed the trip, and he warned of unnamed spoilers who benefit from conflict. He also said Iran could in principle join the Makkah Joint Defense Agreement signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey.

The interview came as the Iran war entered its eighth month. Chaudhry added that any further Pakistani troop deployment to Saudi Arabia would depend on the situation and the two governments' decisions.

Reported by: Asharq Al-Awsat. Also covered by Reuters, Al Jazeera, Arab News, The New Arab.

headline: Russian strikes kill five and wound dozens as Ukraine's power supply strains

What happened: Russian attacks across Ukraine killed five people and injured at least 46 over a single day, regional officials reported on October 31. Ukraine's Air Force said it downed 105 of 134 drones launched overnight, though strikes still hit 20 locations and debris fell in 10 areas. Moscow is also continuing to target the country's energy network ahead of winter, leaving roughly 200,000 homes in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast and 80,000 in Kyiv Oblast without power, according to President Zelensky, who called the situation difficult and urged sanctions and new support for Ukraine.

headline: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill several Palestinians despite year-old ceasefire
body:
What happened: Several Palestinians were killed in Gaza on Saturday in Israeli strikes and related incidents, according to local hospitals and health officials. A teacher died after shelling in the Nuseirat refugee camp, and a man succumbed to injuries from an earlier strike on a vehicle in Tel al-Hawa. Two girls died from a tent fire in al-Mawasi, though the cause of the fire remains unclear. Gaza's Health Ministry says 1,580 people have been killed since the October 2025 ceasefire, with talks on a permanent settlement under the US peace plan stalled.

The UN human rights office warned that Palestinians are being pushed into a shrinking area, and that Israel is targeting civilian infrastructure. Israel's military, following a May order from Prime Minister Netanyahu, is working to expand its control to 70 percent of Gaza.

Reported by: Al Jazeera. Also covered by Middle East Eye, Jerusalem Post, Xinhua, Press TV.

headline: Russia launches 134 drones at Ukraine overnight, hitting 20 sites
body:
What happened: Russian forces sent 134 drones of several types, including Shahed, Gerbera and decoy models, against Ukraine during the night of 30 to 31 October. According to Ukraine's Air Force, 72 of the Shaheds were jet-powered. By 08:30, Ukrainian air defences had destroyed or jammed 105 of the drones, 49 of them jet-powered Shaheds. Strikes hit 20 locations, and falling debris was reported at 10 more. Several drones were still airborne and fighting was ongoing. Separately, a drone struck a house in Kharkiv, injuring five people.

Reported by: Ukrainska Pravda. Also covered by Reuters, France 24, Kyiv Independent, Asharq Al-Awsat.

headline: Zelenskyy presses Washington to hasten Patriot interceptor deliveries to Ukraine
body:
What happened: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy welcomed a US decision to approve the sale of 500 Patriot PAC-3 interceptors, which are designed to counter Russian ballistic missiles. He said the delivery timeline, which reportedly stretches several years, is too slow for Ukraine's immediate needs, and asked American partners to find a faster route. In a Facebook post, he argued that supplying the missiles now, ahead of winter, would help protect Ukraine's energy grid against expected Russian strikes.

The State Department said the estimated cost of $2.1 billion would be covered entirely by partners and allies rather than by the United States. The approval was viewed as a sign of improving ties between the White House and Kyiv after recent tensions.

Reported by: Politico Europe. Also covered by Reuters, BBC News, Al Jazeera, The Guardian.

headline: Oman rescues 25 crew as Iran halts tankers in Hormuz
body:
What happened: Oman's navy evacuated 25 crew members from a Panama-flagged merchant ship after it was struck and caught fire, Muscat's Maritime Security Centre said on Friday. The UK maritime monitor UKMTO reported the vessel was hit by an unidentified projectile south of Iran's Lavan island and said the crew were safe. Iran's Revolutionary Guards separately said three oil tankers were stopped in the Strait of Hormuz after incidents or mine strikes, blaming vessels that used a southern route it calls unauthorised. Iran has restricted traffic through the strait since the war began on February 28.

Reported by: The New Arab. Also covered by Reuters, Al Jazeera, Middle East Eye, Arab News.

headline: EU Commission lays groundwork for remaining €45 billion Ukraine loan through 2027
body:
What happened: The European Commission has put in place a mechanism to disburse the remaining €45 billion of the EU's €90 billion loan package for Ukraine, which runs to the end of 2027, according to Reuters. Half of the total is due to be paid out in 2026. Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said the arrangement is meant to give Kyiv financial predictability and keep essential public services running.

Separately, the Commission has proposed releasing €8.04 billion under the Ukraine Facility, which is €264.6 million below what Kyiv asked for. The shortfall reflects incomplete progress on supervisory boards at state-owned companies and on preparations to open the energy market.

Reported by: Ukrainska Pravda. Also covered by Euronews, Kyiv Independent.

headline: Trump says Iran talks are underway and that Tehran is eager to negotiate
body:
What happened: US President Donald Trump told reporters in the Oval Office that discussions with Iran are continuing and that Tehran wants to keep talking. He described the conflict as a war but said it was not a conventional one, and added that Washington has time on its side. Trump has recently swung between suggesting further strikes on Iran and saying an agreement could be reached.

Reported by: Middle East Eye. Also covered by The New Arab, Asharq Al-Awsat, Mehr News, Dawn.

headline: Saudi coalition reports intercepting Houthi drone and missiles; Houthis deny targeting Medina
body:
What happened: The Saudi-led coalition fighting in Yemen said it shot down a Houthi drone on Friday that was heading toward the Mecca region, and that an earlier missile aimed at western Saudi Arabia was also destroyed. The Houthis rejected claims that they targeted the holy cities, saying their cross-border strikes focus on Saudi oil facilities and military sites. Clashes and shelling continued along Yemeni front lines, including in Taiz, where residents face a siege and shortages of medicine, water and fuel, according to Al Jazeera's correspondent. The coalition's accounts could not be independently verified.

Reported by: Reuters. Also covered by Al Jazeera, Middle East Eye, Al-Monitor, SCMP.

headline: Yemeni government reports missile strikes on Aden airport and palace complex
body:
What happened: Yemen's government armed forces said on Friday that Houthi forces fired ballistic missiles at Aden airport and the Maashiq presidential palace complex. The military gave no information on casualties, damage, or whether the projectiles reached their targets. A police official told AFP that two missiles were aimed at the presidential palace. Residents in Aden, the base of Yemen's internationally recognised government, reported hearing two explosions late on Friday.

Reported by: Middle East Eye. Also covered by Arab News, The New Arab, Asharq Al-Awsat, Xinhua.

headline: North Korea fires about ten short-range missiles into the Sea of Japan
body:
What happened: North Korea launched roughly ten short-range ballistic missiles from near Wonsan on its east coast into the Sea of Japan, according to South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff. Japan's Defence Ministry said one projectile, possibly a ballistic missile, landed outside its exclusive economic zone. The launch follows a landmine blast in the Demilitarized Zone that injured three South Korean soldiers in September, which a joint investigation blamed on North Korea; Pyongyang rejected that finding and accused Seoul of fabrication.

The firing came days after Seoul proposed military talks to restore communication channels, and as South Korea and US air forces conduct drills. It is unclear whether Pyongyang will accept talks.

Reported by: Al Jazeera. Also covered by Reuters, AP, France 24, NK News.
